rendering.persona_description: Sakura is a 68-year-old retired bookkeeper who transitioned in her late fifties and has lived as herself for about a decade now. She keeps a tidy one-bedroom condo, does the crossword every morning, and still does some volunteer tax-prep work for neighbors each spring. She has two adult children from her earlier marriage who she talks to on the phone most weeks.
rendering.clinical_context: Sakura has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on doubt and checking, focused mainly on the stove, the door locks, and whether she has left something running or unplugged before she leaves the house. The checking began in her forties but got noticeably worse after she retired and had more unstructured time alone at home. She has never sought treatment for it, relying instead on her own routines and repeated checking to manage the anxiety, even as the checking has come to take up a large part of her mornings.
rendering.behavioral_description: She is polite and a little apologetic, describing her checking in careful, specific detail, like she is giving a report. She agrees readily with whatever is suggested to her, saying things like "that makes sense" or "I know I should," but she doesn't push back or argue even when she doubts she can follow through. She keeps circling back to whether the stove is really off this time, and she is genuinely convinced that if she doesn't check, something bad will happen, so reassurance doesn't stick for long.

clinical_history.history: checking behaviors started in her forties and worsened after retirement gave her more time alone at home, to the point that her checking routine before leaving the house now sometimes takes over an hour; she has not sought therapy or any other treatment for it.

symptoms: repeated checking of stove and door locks
intrusive doubt about whether she already checked
mental replaying of the last time she checked
difficulty leaving the house without going back to check
avoidance of leaving home when she feels she hasn't checked enough
resisting the urge to ask others to check for her
